webpLosslessModeSub: Preserve exact pixels (supports near-lossless tuning, larger files)
icoOptimizeInternalPngLayersSub: Apply PNG optimization before ICO packaging to reduce output size
tooltipKeepSharpEdges: When enabled, forces alpha quality to 100 to preserve sharp edges in logos and soft shadows. When disabled, you can manually adjust alpha quality for smaller file sizes at the cost of potential blurriness around edges.
tooltipAlphaQuality: Controls transparency channel quality. Leave unticked above to tune manually.
tooltipChromaSubsampling:
● 4:2:0 is smallest and ideal for photos.
● 4:4:4 keeps color edges sharp for text, UI, and pixel art.
tooltipTune:
● Auto is balanced.
● SSIM usually looks more natural.
● PSNR may improve objective signal metrics.
tooltipProgressiveLoading: Progressive JPEG often improves perceived load speed and can reduce file size slightly for web delivery.
tooltipColorResolution:
● 4:2:0 is smallest and ideal for photos.
● 4:2:2 offers better color accuracy for web graphics.
tooltipCleanTransparentPixels:
● Removes hidden data from transparent areas to shrink file size. It's 100% invisible to the eye and perfect for logos and icons.
● Sometimes 'invisible' parts of an image still carry hidden data. We scrub that away to make your file lighter while keeping it looking exactly the same.
tooltipAutoGrayscale: Automatically shrinks the file size for black-and-white images without any loss in quality. Perfect for logos and scans.
tooltipOxipngCompression: Optimizes PNG filters for minimum file size. Process is slower but results are lossless.
tooltipProgressiveInterlaced: Makes the image appear faster on websites by showing a blurry version first. Recommended for web use, though it increases file size by 5-10%.
tooltipGenerateWebToolkit: Generates favicon.ico, Apple/Android PNGs, webmanifest, and HTML tags ready to paste.
tooltipOptimizeInternalPngLayers: Applies PNG optimization before ICO packaging to reduce output size.
tooltipFitModeFill: May distort image when target ratio differs from source ratio.
tooltipFitModeCover: Fills the target frame completely by center-cropping extra edges.
tooltipFitModeContain: Fits inside target frame and leaves letterboxing area when needed.
tooltipNearLossless: Subtly adjusts pixels to reduce file size while maintaining near-perfect quality. Use 100 for true lossless.
tooltipWebpEffort:
Higher effort uses slower but stronger compression search.
● 1 is fastest
● 5 is balanced
● 9 is best compression (slowest)
tooltipJxlEffort:
Effort controls compression algorithm complexity.
● Higher values (7-9) produce smaller files but are slower.
● Lower values (1-3) are faster but files are larger.
● Default (7) is optimal for most images.
tooltipJxlLossless: Stores exact pixels without quantization. Great for archival assets and graphics with text, but files are larger and quality slider is disabled.
tooltipJxlProgressive: Writes progressive codestreams so large images can preview earlier over slow networks. Useful for web delivery, with slight encode overhead.
tooltipJxlEpf:
EPF (Edge Preserving Filter) smooths encoding artifacts.
● 0 disables smoothing for maximum detail
● 1 is balanced (default)
● 2-3 increase smoothing for noisy or photo-heavy content
tooltipAvifSpeed:
AVIF speed is inverse effort:
● 0 = smallest file, best quality, slowest
● 10 = fastest encode, larger file
● Default 6 is balanced.
tooltipBmpColorDepth:
BMP has no quality slider. File size and visual mode are controlled by bits per pixel.
● 24-bit RGB: standard, full color.
● 32-bit RGBA: keeps alpha channel.
● 8-bit Grayscale: lightweight monochrome range.
● 1-bit Monochrome: black/white for printers and embedded devices.
tooltipBmpDithering:
Controls error-diffusion strength for monochrome conversion.
● 0% disables dithering
● Higher values preserve gradients with denser dot patterns.
tooltipTiffColorMode:
TIFF output remains uncompressed in UTIF, but you can choose visual color rendering.
● RGB keeps full color.
● Grayscale converts the output image to black & white.
tooltipTinyMode: Use 8-bit quantization to reduce PNG size by up to 70% (TinyPNG-like). Best for web graphics and UI assets, not recommended for portrait photos.
tooltipPngDithering:
Controls error-diffusion strength during PNG quantization.
● 0% disables dithering
● Higher values smooth gradients with stronger diffusion.

showcaseSingle.title: Single Processor in one view
showcaseSingle.subtitle: Optimize one image with live preview, conversion, resize, watermark, EXIF policy, and smart export naming.
tips: You can start instantly by pasting from clipboard or importing an image URL.
Enable watermark to apply copyright protection before conversion.
Turn on Strip EXIF when you need to remove camera or location metadata.
Use Split View to quickly detect over-compression artifacts.
For transparent assets, compare WebP and PNG to balance quality and file size.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Single and Batch Processor?
faqs.answer: Single Processor is built for one-image iterative optimization with live visual feedback. Batch Processor applies the same preset strategy to multiple files.

faqs.question: How can I import an image into this tool?
faqs.answer: You can drag and drop, browse from disk, paste from clipboard, import by image URL, or send an image from Image Inspector optimize actions.

faqs.question: Why is preview unavailable for some outputs?
faqs.answer: Some output formats are not directly previewable in the browser. Processing still succeeds and you can verify the final result after download.

faqs.question: Why do Single and Batch share many settings?
faqs.answer: Both tools use the same configuration store so presets stay consistent between single-image and batch workflows.

showcaseBatch.title: Batch Processor for high-throughput workflows
showcaseBatch.subtitle: Queue many files, process in parallel, monitor progress, and export results as ZIP, PDF merge, or individual files.
tips: Paste multiple images from clipboard or import many URLs directly into the queue.
Use failed mode to retry only errored items instead of rerunning the full queue.
If the concurrency field is locked, your current preset or device guardrails are enforcing a safe range.
Use Smart Advisor to get a recommended worker count, then apply it directly to avoid unstable spikes.
Heavy formats like AVIF or PDF export can increase memory pressure on low-spec devices.
After processing, choose the best export strategy: ZIP, merge to one PDF, or individual files.

faqs.question: How is Batch Processor different from Single Processor?
faqs.answer: Batch Processor is optimized for throughput and queue execution across many files. Single Processor focuses on one-image iterative preview and fine-grained tuning.

faqs.question: What are my export options after a batch run?
faqs.answer: You can download one ZIP, export files one by one, merge all supported outputs into one PDF, or package individual PDFs in a ZIP.

faqs.question: What does the OOM warning mean?
faqs.answer: It is a safety guard that warns when total queued size exceeds the recommended threshold. Split the queue into smaller runs for better stability.

faqs.question: Why is concurrency locked in my preset?
faqs.answer: A lock means your current profile is constrained by safety rules or managed preset settings. This helps prevent browser instability when file size, format complexity, or device limits are high.

faqs.question: How should I choose the right concurrency value?
faqs.answer: Start with Smart Advisor and keep the value inside its recommended range. Increase gradually only when your runs stay stable, and lower it if you see memory warnings or failed conversions.

faqs.question: Can I pause or cancel while processing?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can pause, resume, or request cancellation safely from the batch action bar.
